content.jointProblem: Can a lightweight content-based recommender, optionally augmented with within-basket co-occurrence, outperform best-seller sorting for one Harmat client with only 500–2,000 transactions? The first experiment would test transfer from the researcher’s clothing-retail point-of-sale study to product-page recommendations using a chronological holdout, comparing best-seller, content-only and hybrid approaches before considering an online pilot.

rationale.text: The researcher has directly relevant work combining product attributes and basket co-occurrence for recommendation under sparse user histories.

sources.quote: A weighted combination of cosine attribute similarity and within-session co-occurrence frequency is used to score candidate recommendations.
The study highlights that even minimal session data meaningfully stabilises recommendation quality when transaction histories per user are fewer than five.

rationale.text: Her recommendation study includes an empirical comparison against a content-only baseline, providing a starting point for comparative evaluation rather than assuming that a hybrid will help.

sources.quote: yielding a precision at three of 0.38 against a pure content baseline of 0.29.

rationale.text: She uses R and Python and has experience preparing and anonymising company data, which is relevant to constructing the pilot dataset.

sources.quote: Za analizu koristi softverske pakete R i Python
sarađivala je kao eksterna analitičarka s jednim regionalnim SaaS provajderom na pripremi i anonimizaciji podataka o ugovorima za potrebe istraživanja.

constraints.text: Evaluation must use the existing small datasets and include best-seller sorting as a baseline; a plan dependent on accumulating substantially more transactions would not meet the task.

sources.quote: The largest dataset had 1 900 completed orders over eighteen months; the smallest had around 520.
Simple best-seller sorting actually outperformed the model in our A/B test on the one client where we got far enough to test.
We do not have the budget or the traffic to wait for larger datasets.

constraints.text: Keep the initial deliverable to a one-client prototype and fit integration work within roughly one developer-day per week.

sources.quote: A working prototype for one client would be enough to start.
We can allocate one mid-level developer for roughly one day per week to an applied research collaboration

constraints.text: Data access must remain within the agreed anonymised transaction and catalogue scope and be covered by a data-sharing agreement.

sources.quote: We can give a collaborator full read access to anonymised transaction and product catalogue data.
access to anonymised client datasets under a data-sharing agreement.

constraints.text: Any deployed widget must fit the company's existing e-commerce integration and client-VPS environment, and user-facing strings must pass its three-language release workflow.

sources.quote: WooCommerce and custom REST API integrations
Docker for containerised deployments on client VPS environments
we test every user-facing string in all three languages before a build ships

constraints.text: The project must accommodate her active dissertation work and preference for collaborations that support her thesis; a schedule cannot be assumed before she confirms capacity.

sources.quote: Dunja Simić je u aktivnoj fazi pisanja doktorske disertacije i preferira saradnje koje se mogu uključiti u okvir njene teze

risks: The relevant recommendation study used 9,200 baskets across two clothing retailers, substantially more data than each target client. Its results may not transfer to 500–2,000 transactions; the first experiment must test this at the client's actual data scale.

Point-of-sale basket proximity is not equivalent to product-page browsing intent. The first experiment must test product-conditioned recommendations, rather than treating basket-level results as validation of an online widget.
The published comparison was against a content-only baseline, not best-seller sorting. Neither its reported precision nor its selected blending weight establishes an advantage for Harmat.

Catalogue attribute completeness, catalogue languages, basket identifiers and historical product availability are unknown. Poor metadata or missing basket structure could undermine both content and hybrid methods.
Low traffic may prevent a timely, conclusive online test; offline ranking improvements would not establish conversion or revenue gains.
Researcher availability is unknown, and this retail recommendation task may not support her subscription-focused dissertation sufficiently to secure sustained participation.
The company's numerical budget, pilot deadline, hosting limits and experience managing a formal research collaboration remain unresolved.
questions: Can the researcher confirm availability, expected effort and whether this recommendation project can fit alongside or support her dissertation?
Which client will host the pilot, and what are its product count, basket-size distribution, repeat-purchase rate and available transaction dates?
Do the anonymised exports retain order-level item groupings, timestamps and stable product identifiers? Are page-view or session logs available, or must the experiment use orders alone?
Which catalogue attributes and description languages are available, and can historical availability, discontinued products and stock exclusions be reconstructed?

Can the first experiment compare best-seller, content-only and hybrid rankings on a chronological holdout without future-data leakage, and what minimum improvement and coverage would justify an online pilot?
What did the previous A/B test measure, and are its allocation, duration, sample sizes and results available for designing the new evaluation?
What budget, deadline, VPS resources and serving-latency limits apply, and who will own integration, maintenance and experiment monitoring?
What data-sharing, retention, access-control, publication and intellectual-property terms must be agreed before work begins?
